row.notes: mov rax,[rax+0x2c0] in Career_Weekends_BuildResultNodes, 7 bytes, no branch lands inside it. rax = the round's TrackDataRecord: items[track*0x10+8] of TrackDataSystem +0x28 ([[param_1+0x40]+0xf58], the CareerEntity TrackDataSystem), track = movzx edi, byte [Weekend+0x278] (edi stays live), Weekend from vt+0x158 of the career's entrant list. rax is 0 when the track's item is empty, as for Paul Ricard (stat id 1) which F1 25 does not ship, and the instruction faults reading 0x2c0 at F1_25.exe+0x181b859 (R&D table, Team HQ). The next instructions (lea rcx,[rax+8]; test rax,rax; cmovz rcx,rbp) already take rax 0 to the empty node handle. Core resumes at +7 with rax 0 and rdi = track. Crash 1571544543059382333 (AnakinGTI, My Team season 2 Team HQ): rdi=0x54 is past the track list, the stale item's record held a wild node pointer 0x1110000000 and lea rcx,[rax+8]; mov rax,[rcx] at 0x14181b87a faulted. Core also resumes with rax 0 for a track id past the list ([[r14+0x40]+0xf58] +0x28/+0x30, 16-byte items), an unreadable record +0x2c0 or an unreadable node first word.

verify.notes: Crash reports n31s (V4xMerstappen, Team HQ) and n34q (Alexandr_Khavrov, R&D table): rax=0 at 0x14181b859, rdi=1 (rcx=0x10 = track 1 << 4), the preceding bytes mov rax,[rax+rcx+8] from TrackDataSystem items. The code after the site tests rax, so resuming at +7 with rax 0 is the game's own empty-node path.
